name.text: Trigonometric Functions — identifying sin, cos, or tan from its graph (JSXGraph)

questiontext.text:
The graph below shows a trigonometric function for \(0 \leq x \leq 2\pi\), with \(x\) in radians.

[[jsxgraph width="400px" height="260px"]] (function() { var funcidx = {#funcidx#}; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-0.6, 3, 7, -3], axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); b.create('axis', [[0,0],[1,0]], {ticks:{visible:false}}); b.create('axis', [[0,0],[0,1]], {ticks:{insertTicks:false, ticksDistance:1, minorTicks:0}}); var lab = ['π/2', 'π', '3π/2', '2π']; for (var i = 1; i <= 4; i++) { b.create('segment', [[i*Math.PI/2, -0.1], [i*Math.PI/2, 0.1]], {strokeColor:'black', fixed:true}); b.create('text', [i*Math.PI/2, -0.35, lab[i-1]], {anchorX:'middle', fixed:true}); } var opt = {strokeColor:'#003399', strokeWidth:2}; if (funcidx === 0) { b.create('functiongraph', [function(x){ return Math.sin(x); }, 0, 2*Math.PI], opt); } else if (funcidx === 1) { b.create('functiongraph', [function(x){ return Math.cos(x); }, 0, 2*Math.PI], opt); } else { b.create('functiongraph', [function(x){ return Math.tan(x); }, 0, Math.PI/2 - 0.12], opt); b.create('functiongraph', [function(x){ return Math.tan(x); }, Math.PI/2 + 0.12, 3*Math.PI/2 - 0.12], opt); b.create('functiongraph', [function(x){ return Math.tan(x); }, 3*Math.PI/2 + 0.12, 2*Math.PI], opt); } })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Which function is shown?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Each basic trigonometric graph has features you can read off directly.

  • \(y = \sin x\) starts at \(0\) when \(x = 0\) and rises first, reaching its maximum \(1\) at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Its period is \(2\pi\).
  • \(y = \cos x\) starts at its maximum \(1\) when \(x = 0\) and falls first. Its period is \(2\pi\).
  • \(y = \tan x\) also starts at \(0\), but it is unbounded and has vertical asymptotes (breaks in the graph) at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) and \(x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\), where \(\cos x = 0\). Its period is \(\pi\), so two branches appear on \([0, 2\pi]\).

The graph shown is \(y = {@ta_tex@}\).

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.9 (Trigonometric Functions). Identifies sin, cos, or tan from the shape of its JSXGraph-plotted graph, including recognising the vertical asymptotes of tan. No diagnostic node: a dropdown classification with a single concept-level hint.

falsefeedback.text: Look at the value of the graph at \(x = 0\), whether it rises or falls first, and whether the graph has breaks (vertical asymptotes).
